correctness.rationale: With four unit-capacity schools, four students and a uniformly random common strict preference, for a fixed student serial order rho each school s is assigned to each rank t with probability 1/4, hence conditional expected justified envy equals (1/4) sum_s KT(rho, pi_s). A fresh independent C++ program enumerated all 24^4=331776 ordered priority quadruples and each of the 24 serial orders, reproducing all 13 optimal-score counts and all 9 nonzero optimal-multiplicity counts; total sum of K=2488608 and unique optimum frequency=51192. Therefore E[min envy]=8641/4608; a uniformly random order yields 3 for every fixed priority profile. A score-constant adjacency swap proves K=12 iff each unordered student pair is split exactly two-versus-two, occurring 2376 times.
residual_risks: Uniform common preferences and independently uniform strict priorities are essential; the mean does not describe arbitrary school markets.
The finite program enumerates the entire specified space; C++ uses integer comparisons and checks histogram totals.

value.rationale: The complete first small four-school risk spectrum is a natural finite invariant of optimal fairness under uncertain common preferences, including frequencies of unique ties and of zero improvement. Its joint distribution is not implied by the mechanism-to-Kemeny theorem and is useful for exact benchmarks.
residual_risks: Small-market exact law, no asymptotic market-size conclusion.
